scores.evidence: opener gives context before verdict; 'hinged on a decision made while the cars were standing still' is a tease, not a sharp evaluative claim
'He recovered the positions, made the tyres work and, when the race finally brought Russell within reach, completed the pass' — explicit summary paragraph restating the argument
'Behind the Mercedes pair, Verstappen made the most...' and 'Ferrari also left its home race with little to celebrate' are bridging sentences, not abrupt transitions
3.857s, 13.7s, 0.264s, 0.85s/lap, 7.1s, 1m23.504s cluster repeatedly; multiple figures per paragraph rather than one surgical number per claim

'His late-race pace suggests he would still have caught Russell rapidly, but catching him before the finish would have been a much bigger ask' — hedged, but 'does not make the result inevitable in either direction' collapses into false neutrality
Russell is the default benchmark throughout; Antonelli's pace, strategy and pass all measured against his teammate first
Race-control log entries used ('CAR 12 (ANT) TIME 1:28.582 DELETED') but no radio, team comms or driver quotes; evidentiary punctuation is thin and mechanical rather than complicating the reading
'He slipped to second by lap two, sixth by lap 10 and seventh at the finish' — sequential running-order recap; 'Antonelli had qualified seventh before a 12-place grid penalty' re-narrates known facts
Almost no dry irony; 'For Russell, second place was a frustrating return' is plain statement; closest thing to understatement is 'little to celebrate' — flat but not genuinely comic or ironic
First person absent entirely; no judgment calls flagged, no genuine surprise registered; personality as accent is missing altogether
Gasly, Pérez, Tsunoda named without introduction; VSC mechanics, track-limits procedure assumed known; no hand-holding

'That does not make the result inevitable in either direction. Traffic, tyre wear and the timing of a green-flag stop could all have changed the calculation. What is clear is...' — three-sentence paragraph making two or three points and not exiting cleanly
'A lap later, he was through' works; but many paragraphs run long sentences against long sentences with no short punch to answer them
VSC mechanism section gets appropriate room; but the final Ferrari/Pérez/Tsunoda paragraph crams too many events into equal density, and the summary coda is longer than warranted

top_fixes: Kill the final paragraph entirely — it is a textbook summary restatement; the piece should end at 'Madrid' or on the Verstappen/Ferrari coda with no reprise of Antonelli's arc

Strip one number from every multi-figure paragraph and deploy the surviving one as a hard stop rather than part of a data list; the 0.85s/lap figure should land alone, not inside a sentence already carrying 7.1s and 0.264s

Insert first-person once — flag the extrapolation ('I make that roughly 37 laps of recovery at normal racing pace, with 25 to go') rather than presenting the arithmetic as neutral fact; the absence of any voiced judgment call is the single biggest AI tell
